title: Guest Docker workloads, recursive VMs and host isolation
objective: CURRENT ACTIVE WORK (2026-11-01): verify guest Docker workloads, nested VM boot and the repeated host-isolation/egress boundary for the VM-first release. Local nested HTTP/CONNECT proxy chaining and `.bench-models` snapshot exclusion are implemented/tested; owner-host nested acceptance remains open. Coordinate phased execution through #35 and do not claim the local guest's KVM checks as CachyOS host evidence.

acceptance_criteria.text: From the guest agent, bring up a representative project Compose stack (including PostgreSQL), run its tests, stop/restart services, and tear down the stack without requiring host Docker or host-side compose orchestration.

Guest-local ports, bind mounts within the selected guest workspace, volumes and ordinary Compose features work for guest workloads; no generated restrictive compose overlay silently blocks normal project behavior.

Host isolation remains intact: no host Docker socket, no host route/LAN exposure, no access to host files outside the selected workspace, and no host credential directory mount. Services do not publish onto the host LAN.

QEMU restrict=on remains enforced for outer and nested VMs. Guest/workload public HTTP(S) uses only the proxy; blank allowed_domains permits public hosts, while the proxy rejects non-public/mixed DNS and parent-local/directly connected networks. Direct guest Internet/DNS, non-HTTP, host/LAN, and ancestor routes remain blocked; the Linux route guard fails closed if host routes cannot be inspected. Broader public egress is owner-approved.

When nested virtualization is available, the guest can launch and control a nested Little Mester VM with an explicitly selected guest-side workspace, run a test there, and stop it. Capability absence is detected and reported without weakening the outer boundary.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: 2026-11-02 owner-host report vm-acceptance-20261102T142613Z-1204519-dbe140e7.json: existing nested child answered SSH, passed depth-1 cloud-init/context/virtiofs/workspace readiness; depth-cap probe ran from the child and refused depth 2 before state; outer continuity passed. No representative guest workload or nested-VM stop was performed, so the criterion is partial.

acceptance_criteria.text: Lifecycle distinguishes ordinary guest workload cleanup from outer-VM deletion; it does not silently delete active recursive test state or evidence, and any destructive teardown is explicit.
Tests cover Compose feedback loops, host-boundary negative cases, current egress allow/deny policy and nested-VM capability/boot behavior; evidence is recorded before claiming support.

Recursive Little Mester execution is opt-in, uses a separate disposable workspace/state, and enforces the propagated maximum nesting depth (default 0) before starting child agents/VMs. Neither recurse nor unsafe-recurse grants additional host paths, host Docker, credentials, LAN, or broader egress; self-write authority requires explicit unsafe-recurse. See #52.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Local Bats tests cover explicit opt-in, depth/default/boundaries, pre-prerequisite over-depth refusal, snapshot isolation, host-state exclusions, symlink refusal, and explicit live-profile cleanup refusal. Local mocks do not establish nested KVM, virtiofs, or host-isolation acceptance. Owner-host report vm-acceptance-20261102T142613Z-1204519-dbe140e7.json also confirms depth-1 child readiness, excluded `.mester` host control state in the child workspace, depth-2 refusal before state creation, and parent continuity. It does not prove all host-path/credential/Docker/LAN/egress boundaries or direct-agent self-write behavior; those remain open.

Repeat the non-public destination and allowlist matrix inside the live guest and rootless workload network on the owner KVM host; verify QEMU restrict=on, host gateway/LAN/direct Internet negative paths, selected model/proxy guestfwd positive paths, and host workspace/credential boundary. This environment lacks /dev/kvm and cannot substitute local unit tests for host acceptance.

Repeat the same positive/negative matrix from a nested VM before claiming recursion. Preserve the existing overlay; no firewall/route changes.
On an unsupported nested-virtualization guest, verify usable /dev/kvm preflight refuses before workspace copy, VM provision, or agent startup.

On a supported owner KVM host, launch nested profile at depth 1, verify child receives the incremented depth and inherited maximum, then verify another child refuses before startup; verify nested VM uses its own QEMU restrict=on/proxy allowlist and host/private/LAN negative checks.

Live-test nested child workspace and VM-state separation, preservation of the parent workspace/session, stop/reuse semantics, and confirmed recursion-clean teardown; local copy tests do not establish virtiofs/KVM isolation.

For safe top-level repository snapshots, verify recursion-clean initial-<profile> refuses while the associated outer VM profile is running, then removes the snapshot only after the outer VM is stopped; verify normal nested-profile cleanup also refuses live QEMU/virtiofsd/proxy processes.

Owner-host acceptance must verify --discard-recursive behavior on a disposable recursive profile, including preserving/inspecting child evidence before explicit discard; do not use the working host-Docker session or a valuable overlay.

Before write-enabled `--unsafe-recurse`, prove the shared Little Mester checkout cannot expose `.mester/vm/<profile>` host VM state/control keys to the guest. Current virtiofs workspace contains `.mester/vm/default/id_vm_control` (mode 0600, owned by the same mester UID); move VM state outside the share or enforce an equivalent exclusion, then test the child boundary. Do not use the live checkout for unsafe recursion until resolved.

Preserve model files. In outer guest read-only inspect df -h / and the exact $HOME/.cache/lab-vm-recursion/recursion-smoke staging tree; verify no .workspace-* partial and adequate free space, do not delete it if present until evidence reviewed. If clean, rerun only env LAB_VM_RECURSION_DEPTH=0 LAB_VM_MAX_DEPTH=1 ./lab-vm up recursion-smoke --workspace /workspace --recurse (no agent/model request). If still ENOSPC or stale state exists, stop and return redacted output; no down/recursion-clean/manual recursive cache deletion. Then verify child policy/context depth1/max1, over-depth refusal before state/startup, and parent session continuity. #35 model/ERRCONN gate remains deferred by owner request; this shell-only test does not pass agent/TUI/model or nested egress/isolation acceptance.

CURRENT NESTED EGRESS PLAN (2026-11-01): the child cloud-init request reached its proxy and got 502, while the outer guest's same public request via parent 10.0.2.100:3128 returned 200. Child is stopped and its proxy port/listener is gone. Before another host retry, locally audit/fix nested proxy routing: only nested VM proxy processes chain HTTP and CONNECT to the existing parent guestfwd proxy 10.0.2.100:3128; top-level proxy remains direct. Child permission=false/allowed_domains must be enforced before chaining; parent must remain the final public-only destination validator (mixed DNS, private/non-public, host-local/directly connected networks denied). Keep nested QEMU restrict=on; no direct routes, host sockets, model changes, or allowlist broadening. Add local tests proving public request/CONNECT forwarding, child-deny makes no upstream request, parent 403 is preserved, and top-level configuration does not chain. After local tests, sync into active safe snapshot and use a NEW disposable child profile for one host boot/depth-boundary run. Successful apt alone is not nested-isolation acceptance: separately test public HTTP(S) through proxy, direct egress/DNS, private/LAN/ancestor targets, and QEMU restrict=on from child; preserve all evidence and keep cleanup separate.

CURRENT RELEASE PHASE — 2026-11-01: owner configured max recursion depth 2. Before a live child run, implement/check resource fit; this guest has ~3.8GiB RAM and runner currently requests 4GiB per VM. Once safe, prove allowed depth1/depth2 child and over-depth refusal before state/QEMU; inspect source state/secret exclusions and parent continuity.

Separate live boundary gate still required: child positive HTTP/HTTPS CONNECT via its own policy and parent proxy; direct/raw DNS, private/LAN/metadata/ancestor targets denied; parent denials propagate; QEMU restrict=on and exact channels verified; guest and child Compose workloads have no host Docker socket. Apt success or local proxy mocks do not pass this gate.

After the #41 extension is committed/present on CachyOS, run its existing-child `--reuse-child` continuation once to obtain live nested QEMU and child-originated network-boundary evidence. This covers only representative nested egress/isolation checks; it does not establish physical-host LAN/listener isolation, host credentials/files beyond the selected snapshot, guest Compose workload behavior, or explicit stop/reuse/cleanup semantics. Stop on first failure and preserve both VMs/report.

The updated #41 continuation performs host and nested loopback binding checks plus representative guest egress probes. Still separately required for #43: guest/workload attempts to reach parent-local/directly connected, private/LAN, metadata and ancestor targets must be denied; nested positive HTTP/HTTPS via chained proxy, parent denial passthrough, non-HTTP/direct/raw DNS denial, workload Docker-socket absence, Compose feedback and explicit nested stop/cleanup semantics remain unaccepted. No AC status changes from local mocks.

2026-11-02 local host-boundary extension: `lab-vm verify-isolation` now requires the actual profile SSH and egress-proxy TCP sockets to appear in `ss -H -ltn` as IPv4 `127.0.0.1` only, in addition to validating QEMU restrict/forwarding argv. The nested runner first invokes this read-only check against the physical-host outer profile, then repeats it inside the outer VM against the child before continuing child guest probes. It stops before child checks on outer-boundary failure, enforces bounded/sanitized output, and explicitly skips model availability. Per owner decision, this replaces a separate second-device test for inbound QEMU exposure; guest-originated private/LAN egress denial remains required.
